chunks: And in it it is narrated that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers.
Except for those among them who departed from whom he [Satan] gained authority because they obeyed his desire and followed their own whims.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this conditional authority to refute the Mu'tazila and Khawarij extremes, emphasizing that while Satan has a granted lease (*idhnan*) to test humanity, his power is nullified when believers exercise *ikhtiyar* (free will) to remain obedient. This underscores the Shia doctrine that divine grace and human agency work in tandem, where Satan's influence is limited to those who actively choose to follow their lower desires (*hawā*).
